questions.stem: The friable masses seen on this mitral valve specimen most characteristically give rise to which complication?

explanation.summary: The valve shows friable vegetations composed of fibrin, platelets, and microorganisms. Fragments of these lesions readily break off and travel through the systemic circulation, producing septic emboli to organs such as the brain, kidneys, and spleen.
explanation.whyCorrect: The valve shows friable vegetations composed of fibrin, platelets, and microorganisms. Fragments of these lesions readily break off and travel through the systemic circulation, producing septic emboli to organs such as the brain, kidneys, and spleen.

questions.stem: This illustration shows an aortic root complicated by an acute type A aortic dissection. By what mechanism does the depicted lesion produce aortic regurgitation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rheumatic commissural fusion narrowing the valve orifice

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fusion of two congenitally malformed cusps into a bicuspid valve

choices.label: C
choices.text: Calcific fibrosis stiffens and fuses the leaflet cusps

choices.label: D
choices.text: The dissection flap distorts leaflet alignment, preventing valve coaptation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Infective vegetations perforate and destroy the leaflet tissue

explanation.summary: In type A dissection the intimal flap extends into the aortic root and distorts the normal alignment of the aortic valve leaflets, causing malcoaptation so the cusps cannot close completely, which allows diastolic backflow (regurgitation) rather than obstruction or leaflet destruction.
explanation.whyCorrect: In type A dissection the intimal flap extends into the aortic root and distorts the normal alignment of the aortic valve leaflets, causing malcoaptation so the cusps cannot close completely, which allows diastolic backflow (regurgitation) rather than obstruction or leaflet destruction.
